all_findings.title: Threshold-to-SC mapping is correct; 4.5:1 normal-text floor is the right conservative AA assumption for terminal cells
all_findings.claim: The contract's 4.5:1 class (text, dim, info, error, warn; theme.rs:649-654) maps to WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum), Level AA, normal text. The 3.0:1 class (accent, accent2, success, special, dim2; theme.rs:662-667) maps to SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (AA) for graphical/UI elements, and coincides with the SC 1.4.3 large-text floor. sel_fg-on-accent >= 4.5:1 (theme.rs:655-661) is again 1.4.3 for text on the selection-bar bg. The contract is AA, not AAA — SC 1.4.6 (AAA) would require 7:1 normal / 4.5:1 large, which it does not claim ('WCAG 2.x AA', theme.rs:13). The 4.5:1 floor for terminal text is the correct conservative posture: a terminal cell glyph's point size is set by the user's emulator and is unknowable to the application, so the auditor must assume normal-size (<18pt regular / <14pt bold) text; the large-text 3:1 relaxation can never be statically claimed. The luminance/ratio math in the test (theme.rs:606-623) matches the WCAG 2.x definition (sRGB linearization, 0.05 flare term) and matches the independently computed values in audits/.a11yaudit/discovery/contrast-cvd.json. Runtime evidence: the contract test passes.

all_findings.title: Modifier::BOLD on 3.0:1 roles cannot establish the WCAG large-text relaxation — terminal font size is user-controlled, so bold-at-3:1 is only conditionally AA
all_findings.claim: A majority of the readable-text usages of the 3.0:1 roles carry Modifier::BOLD (e.g. ui.rs:237 picker ids accent2+BOLD; ui.rs:454 '· Step {}/3' accent2+BOLD; ui.rs:603/1291/1402/2194 '─── {} ───' group headers accent2+BOLD; ui.rs:918-924 done-TODO full rows success+BOLD; ui.rs:946-952 in-progress TODO rows special+BOLD; ui.rs:1433 account email success+BOLD; ui.rs:1456/1478/1490/1574/1664/1708/1740/1888 '▶ Press Enter…' CTA sentences success+BOLD; ui.rs:2537 agent names accent2+BOLD; ui.rs:2723 Law ids special+BOLD; the Help tab's cy/yl bold styles ui.rs:2807-2808). WCAG 2.2 defines large text as >=18pt regular or >=14pt (~18.66px) bold; ratatui's BOLD maps to the terminal's bold attribute but the glyph point size is whatever the user configured in their emulator. Therefore bold-at-3:1 would be AA-conformant ONLY for users whose terminal font is >=14pt — a condition the application can neither know nor enforce. Flagged as conditional: these sites cannot be reclassified out of the 4.5:1 requirement on the basis of BOLD alone. (Same mitigating fact as T1-F2 applies: actual palette values currently exceed 4.5:1, so no live failure.)

all_findings.title: Omega default-theme exemption is a legitimate conformance posture — EXCEPT warn, which is a hardcoded Rgb(255,165,0) inside the 'adaptive' theme and renders at 1.97:1 on light terminal schemes
all_findings.location: crates/omega-tui/src/theme.rs:169-189 (Omega palette, warn at theme.rs:181), theme.rs:29-33, theme.rs:632-637, theme.rs:429; consumer ui.rs:1237
all_findings.claim: Adjudication of the exemption (theme.rs:632-637, 'only Omega may skip the contract'): delegating contrast to the terminal palette via named ANSI colors with bg=None is the standard, defensible posture for TUIs — it is how most curses/ratatui applications behave, and is analogous to honoring user-configured colors: the user (or their emulator's scheme author) owns the pairing, and any contrast failure is correctable by the user without touching the app. Residual risk class (a), accepted: classic named-ANSI weak pairs on light schemes — e.g. a typical light-scheme yellow renders ~2.51:1 on white (computed for (196,160,0)); this risk genuinely belongs to the terminal scheme. Residual risk class (b), NOT accepted: Omega's warn role is not a named ANSI color — it is hardcoded Rgb(255,165,0) (theme.rs:181, '// warn — the historical blocked-badge orange') inside the otherwise-adaptive palette. On a light terminal background it renders at 1.97:1 (computed, WCAG formula), failing not just the 4.5:1 text floor the contract assigns to warn (theme.rs:654) but even the 3.0:1 non-text floor — and the user has NO palette recourse since it bypasses their scheme. This contradicts both the exemption rationale 'no fixed luminance exists to audit' (theme.rs:30-31 — false for warn, which has fixed luminance and could be contract-tested against representative light/dark bgs) and the blurb 'adapts to your terminal's own scheme' (theme.rs:429). Impact scoping: warn's only call site is the Blocked badge glyph '! ' (ui.rs:1237, bold, 2 chars) → effectively SC 1.4.11 non-text (3:1) rather than 1.4.3, and the state is also encoded by glyph shape ('!' vs '+','~','x'), so it is not color-only — hence medium, not high. Still a real default-theme defect on light schemes: the blocked indicator drops below non-text minimum at 1.97:1.

all_findings.title: Active tab in the top tab bar is signaled by accent hue + BOLD only — no marker glyph or underline
all_findings.claim: The Tabs widget marks the active tab with fg(th::accent())+BOLD against fg(th::dim()) inactive tabs. BOLD is technically a non-color channel, but many terminal emulators render 'bold' as a brighter color with no weight change ('bold-as-bright'), in which case the active-tab indicator collapses to a pure hue/brightness difference. Every other selection surface in the TUI adds a '▶' marker or underline; the tab bar is the only navigation state without a shape/position cue. Low severity: keyboard-driven context plus BOLD nominally satisfies 1.4.1, but it is the weakest signal in the app.

survivors.title: Active tab in the top tab bar is signaled by accent hue + BOLD only — no marker glyph or underline
survivors.claim: The Tabs widget marks the active tab with fg(th::accent())+BOLD against fg(th::dim()) inactive tabs. BOLD is technically a non-color channel, but many terminal emulators render 'bold' as a brighter color with no weight change ('bold-as-bright'), in which case the active-tab indicator collapses to a pure hue/brightness difference. Every other selection surface in the TUI adds a '▶' marker or underline; the tab bar is the only navigation state without a shape/position cue. Low severity: keyboard-driven context plus BOLD nominally satisfies 1.4.1, but it is the weakest signal in the app.

verdict.evidence: Citation verified verbatim: ui.rs:582-593 builds Tabs with .style(Style::default().fg(th::dim())) [line 592] and .highlight_style(Style::default().fg(th::accent()).add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD)) [line 593] — no glyph, underline, bg fill, or custom divider. Single code path: draw_tabs (ui.rs:572) is the only Tabs::new in the file and is called once at ui.rs:75. Mitigation search came up empty: grep for UNDERLINED/REVERSED in ui.rs hits only ui.rs:1218 (chat-panel title cue) and ui.rs:1473 (link style), neither in the tab bar. Comparative claim confirmed: all other selection surfaces use a '▶' marker (ui.rs:223, 288, 351, 385, 612) and/or fg/bg inversion via fg(th::sel_fg()).bg(th::accent()) (ui.rs:228-229, 293-294, 388-389, 615-616), both of which survive bold-as-bright terminal rendering — the tab bar is the only hue+BOLD-only navigation indicator.
